name: Northern Reach
strategic: The iron spine. Hard to invade, harder to leave.
blurb: Mountains, mines, and Alistair's oldest garrisons.

name: Stormlands
blurb: Forests under the fortress that does not bend.

name: Old Borderlands
strategic: Raiders come through here when the crown looks away.
blurb: A bruised edge of the kingdom where loyalty was always optional.

name: Western Forest
strategic: Roads vanish. So do tax collectors.
blurb: Ruined forts and villages that bow last, if they bow at all.

name: Harrowlands
strategic: A large population that remembers older kings than Valen.

name: Dorn Crossing
strategic: Whoever holds the crossing holds the road south from Storm.
blurb: A town that exists because armies must cross water somewhere.

name: Eastern March
strategic: The face Nezrel turns toward Varos.
blurb: Watchtowers, grain, and the memory of a war Erol won twenty years ago.

name: Riverlands
strategic: The roads into Caerlyn run through these fields.
blurb: Wide water, mills, and more food than politics.

name: Caerlyn
strategic: Kings are crowned here. They are also killed here.
special: Court, seal, and the Flame's hearth
blurb: The capital on its rock above the River Vey.

name: Crownlands
strategic: The city's pantry and its first ring of villages.
blurb: Farms that can see the castle on a clear day.

name: Larkspool
strategic: A small seat with a long reach into court.
blurb: House Edevane's polite estate, richer than it looks.

name: Maren Vale
strategic: Horses and harvests. Whoever feeds the war eats from here.
blurb: The eastern estates where Arlo learned to ride.

name: Southern Ports
strategic: Tariffs. Lose them and the treasury notices in a week.
blurb: Docks, warehouses, and sailors who price loyalty.

name: Veyne Coast
strategic: Celene's ships can feed a king or forget him.
blurb: The long southern shore House Veyne actually owns.
